+# B300 execution handoff, 18 October 2026
+
+## Current status
+
+Latest access check at16:42UTC: the user explicitly requested one new connection after reporting restored access. SSH returned its banner and password prompt, but rejected the single password submission with `Permission denied (publickey,gssapi-keyex,gssapi-with-mic,password)` and exit1. No authenticated session, remote command or B300 fit occurred; no retry is scheduled. [Latest access receipt](ACCESS_CHECK_20261018T1642Z.json). The earlier timeout below is retained as history; the current blocker is authentication, whose exact cause remains unknown.
+
+The user authorized execution of the reviewed backlog on all eight B300s through one persistent SSH session. Root made one 90-second attempt to `epanov_s@10.14.14.26`; SSH timed out during banner exchange before authentication. No password was submitted, no remote command ran, no fit started, and no retry is scheduled. See [AUTHORITY.json](AUTHORITY.json) and [ACCESS_CHECK.json](ACCESS_CHECK.json). Remote access is the immediate blocker; current host allocation, UUID availability, topology, driver/CUDA/PyTorch stack, data paths, storage and scheduler remain unverified.
+
+The previous read-only inventory reported eight visible B300s, about 275 GB per device, and three GPUs busy with vLLM processes. That snapshot is not an allocation or current availability receipt. Preserve those workloads. Do not start queue jobs from the example files: [allocation.example.json](../b300_queue_preparation_r1/allocation.example.json) has execution disabled and no UUIDs/resources, and [bound-arms.example.json](../b300_queue_preparation_r1/bound-arms.example.json) has no arms. Every PR in [queue.json](../b300_queue_preparation_r1/queue.json) has `launch_ready=false` and `fit_admitted=false`.
+
+## First source-bound work after access
+
+The only currently source-bound fit recipe is the registered rank-one labels-only comparison, F2/seed1001: fresh GRU H512×1 versus H384×2, two fits. Its exact pointers are [cluster handoff](../priority25_execution_r4/cluster/ISSUE_RANK01_F2.md), [recipe](../priority25_execution_r4/RANK01_RECIPE.json), [trainer argv and staged/resume commands](../priority25_execution_r4/RANK01_COMMANDS.json), source commit `a266b036b02e8e012c6eb31072291dad618a169d`, official grader `6f9fd05e491a9700cce1adf50e58b56cdc5e65bb`, recipe SHA-256 `9292b545fd088df40c4cc54066a745025ee4d30c2bf1574bdb4df341eb16937c`, and F2 manifest SHA-256 `56b0e2ecb6bbda1f34569206cbf2c276544c275bac025793ae450488cf5d17a2`.
+
+Before any profile or fit, bind the actual clean source checkout, cluster-readable data and fold paths, input/cache hashes, output/scratch paths, two free physical GPU UUIDs, software versions and bounded CPU/RAM/GPU/time limits. Verify the exact data hashes in the cluster handoff; those expected values are `train.parquet=4a7756449a4bcf272cf715bb405a2152987041605f6c1cce650243ab2abf4e81`, `valid.parquet=2861ee30914065702626a3ac033d80d0563cdacaea50c667fc828c2eeb418782`, `train_targets.npz=ead1a05e7aa5ac3d1c10cde65986be9f48fd342cadb95330611e58c3a8f817e9`, and `valid_targets.npz=dbb7a1a48dd0af9fa524a80c2694008a56cb91d5dae80e8d0d4984c0c5622955`, with target-index hashes and canonical fold binding from the same handoff. The old `/home/grinchenkoeg/...` paths, Beleriand UUID, 4-GB device cap, systemd wrapper and resource limits are not cluster bindings.
+
+After those values are verified and two devices are actually admitted, run the two exact-shape profiles serially or on distinct admitted UUIDs. This is the RANK01 profile argv with only run name, fold and split path bound to F2; do not add `torchrun`:
+
+```bash
+cd "$SOURCE_ROOT"
+export PYTHONPATH="$SOURCE_ROOT/src"
+export WNN_PROJECT_ROOT="$DATA_ROOT"
+export NVIDIA_TF32_OVERRIDE=0
+
+CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="$WIDE_UUID" "$PYTHON" "$SOURCE_ROOT/scripts/train_rnn.py" \
+  --name rr18_r01_wide_f2_s1001_profile_v1 --hidden 512 --layers 1 \
+  --valid-fold 2 --split-manifest "$SPLITS/fold2.json" --device cuda \
+  --arch gru --cell gru --enc linear --dropout 0 --train-seqs 10607 \
+  --train-source train+valid --valid-train-fraction 1 --valid-repeat 1 \
+  --n-valid-folds 4 --full-valid --eval-source vfold --batch 8 --chunk 2000 \
+  --epochs 6 --checkpoint-policy fixed --checkpoint-epoch 5 \
+  --no-eval-during-fit --seed 1001 --precision fp32 --loss wmse \
+  --loss-norm chunk --batch-order seeded --deterministic --sync-free \
+  --fused-adam --grad-stats --optim adamw --lr 0.0001 --beta2 0.999 \
+  --wd 0.01 --sched onecycle --warmup-frac 0.05 --head-lr-mult 1 \
+  --clip 1 --profile-steps 3 --profile-warmup 1
+
+CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES="$DEEP_UUID" "$PYTHON" "$SOURCE_ROOT/scripts/train_rnn.py" \
+  --name rr18_r01_deep_f2_s1001_profile_v1 --hidden 384 --layers 2 \
+  --valid-fold 2 --split-manifest "$SPLITS/fold2.json" --device cuda \
+  --arch gru --cell gru --enc linear --dropout 0 --train-seqs 10607 \
+  --train-source train+valid --valid-train-fraction 1 --valid-repeat 1 \
+  --n-valid-folds 4 --full-valid --eval-source vfold --batch 8 --chunk 2000 \
+  --epochs 6 --checkpoint-policy fixed --checkpoint-epoch 5 \
+  --no-eval-during-fit --seed 1001 --precision fp32 --loss wmse \
+  --loss-norm chunk --batch-order seeded --deterministic --sync-free \
+  --fused-adam --grad-stats --optim adamw --lr 0.0001 --beta2 0.999 \
+  --wd 0.01 --sched onecycle --warmup-frac 0.05 --head-lr-mult 1 \
+  --clip 1 --profile-steps 3 --profile-warmup 1
+```
+
+`SOURCE_ROOT`, `DATA_ROOT`, `SPLITS`, `PYTHON`, `WIDE_UUID` and `DEEP_UUID` are intentionally unset until measured from the actual admitted host; this block is the exact recipe binding, not evidence a remote run occurred. Require finite profiles, strict FP32, memory headroom and an ownership check before fits. Then follow the pinned stage-1/continuation argv in `RANK01_COMMANDS.json`; keep the fixed epoch-5 endpoint, original labels only, matched runtime and source-qualified F2 membership. The saved commands are exact argv references, not portable Beleriand launch wrappers.
+
+The new `src/wnn/cluster_queue` can schedule independent **one-GPU** jobs after complete arm/source/input/resource/output bindings and a real enabled allocation. It rejects multi-GPU fits. The canonical trainer has no DDP process group, rank/device binding, sequence sharding, global objective reductions, collective metric path or rank-state resume. Eight cards therefore mean at most eight independent one-card jobs, never a `torchrun` wrapper around this trainer. `materialize` currently cannot run against the empty example arm file.
+
+## Reviewed proposals and admission gates
+
+The 16 original PRs plus issue #16 are inventoried below. “Current first gate” is the missing prerequisite before a distinct scientific cell can be materialized; every item still needs actual host/data/source/profile admission. PR submitter metadata does not prove idea authorship; all PRs list the same repository account.
+
+| Item | Proposal / planned fits | Implementation and first missing gate |
+|---|---:|---|
+| PR1 | Causal Transformer output AR; 60 | Proposal only; implement real causal teacher, own-prediction AR/KV path, exporter and matched direct-attention control. No DDP. |
+| PR2 | Cold GRU width/depth compute match; 150 | Existing GRU factory is reusable, but freeze five exact configs, matched measured update/compute budget and threshold; current five one-seed screens do not establish scaling. Distinct from R4’s near-parameter pair. |
+| PR3 | GRU vs Transformer teacher families; 120 | Student trainer reusable; complete Transformer and fold-clean teacher/cache producer first, then identical student recipe and target calibration. |
+| PR4 | Per-field age vs seven group clocks; 60 | Prior short profile/partial evidence only; add rank/optimizer-geometry confound controls and clean FP32 teacher/cache/parent lineage. |
+| PR5 | Function-preserving GRU widening; 60 | Initializer parity and short profile exist; bind clean fold parents, fixed growth implementation, full-budget matched continuation and threshold. |
+| PR6 | Frozen-parent output anchor; 60 | Resource profile only; validate FP32 parent export and separate teacher-function/calibration effects. |
+| PR7 | Causal learned initial-state family; 120 | Subset recipes only; expand beyond 104 sequences, validate prefix timing/gradient semantics and rebuild clean fold parents. |
+| PR8 | Grouped Transformer projection; 60 | Grouped starter only; add flat parameter-matched control, freeze groups/temporal positions and implement/profile Transformer. |
+| PR9 | Past-only smoothing plus raw input; 60 | Helper only; wire feature/cache/stream path, fit coefficient on train only, test prefix/reset invariance. |
+| PR10 | Trailing circle residual; 60 | Coordinate meaning unresolved; freeze pairs/window/epsilon and validate degeneracy, cancellation and causal-prefix behavior. |
+| PR11 | Chronos/TimesFM transfer; 60 | No eligible checkpoint/adapter binding; resolve task-rule eligibility, license/hash/pretraining scope and causal multivariate target mapping. |
+| PR12 | Clean heterogeneous teacher cohort; 60 | One F3 teacher/export exists; rebuild clean FP32 cohort per fold and bind each ancestry/cache and fixed mixture coefficient. |
+| PR13 | Fixed checkpoint trajectory average; 60 | Two F0 averages constructed, export/grade pending; rebind fixed epoch/norm across all fold/seed endpoints. |
+| PR14 | Causal innovation residuals; 60 | Prior pair blocked on cache schema; fix producer/consumer fixtures and bind fold-clean FP32 predictors/inputs. |
+| PR15 | Causal geometry/discrete features; 120 / 15 theoretical waves | Four arms and feature ranges are specified; first gates are exact source/data manifests, clean source binding, 8-card profile and 5,371,320-update resource projection. No B300 update measurement exists. |
+| PR17 | Causal smoother GRU teachers + distillation; 330 / 42 theoretical waves | No PyTorch smoke/profile/teacher registry/cache. Test full 112-sequence H1024×2 Python-loop trainer, bind fold-clean producer/checkpoint/cache identities and full-cost budget first. |
+| Issue #16 | R4 rank-1 labels-only F2/seed1001 wide/deep; **2** | Closest runnable basis: exact trainer, recipe, grader, fold and target-cache hashes above. Still blocked by SSH/data/ownership/actual B300 profiles; one pair is not CP30. |
+
+### Ranked-25 items and mapping
+
+Ranks order hypotheses, not executable jobs. “Adjacent” or “scaffold” does not mean a PR implements the hypothesis; items without PRs require new implementation and matched controls.
+
+| Rank | Idea | PR relation | Admission dependency |
+|---:|---|---|---|
+| 1 | Wide/shallow GRU convergence | PR2 exact family; R4 is a separate near-parameter recipe | Matched measured-compute recipe and full FP32 budget. |
+| 2 | Causal prefix statistics/normalization with raw bypass | PR9/14/15/17 adjacent but distinct | Explicit raw → raw+statistics → normalized+raw control sequence. |
+| 3 | Strong causal teacher to compact student | PR1/3/12/17 broad direction | Official student endpoint, clean teacher ancestry and calibration. |
+| 4 | Intermediate teacher hidden-state hints | None | Freeze teacher/student and projected hint control; audit semantic query. |
+| 5 | Output-component capacity | None | Parameter match and score reconstructed outputs. |
+| 6 | Shared transforms with feature IDs | PR8 adjacent | Within-group sharing + ID/escape is unimplemented. |
+| 7 | i1 reliability / inter-instrument lags | PR4 adjacent only | Compare no-i1, i1 and fixed lag basis. |
+| 8 | Local causal attention plus recurrence | PR1 adjacent only | Same backbone with and without fixed left-causal window. |
+| 9 | Covariance orientation | PR15 adjacent only | Causal covariance vs trace/activity controls. |
+| 10 | Mamba-3 MIMO vs SISO teacher | None | Streaming/reset/causal parity, matched capacity and same student. |
+| 11 | xLSTM matrix-memory teacher | None | Scalar/matrix memory match and same student transfer. |
+| 12 | Nonlinear metric calibration | None | Low-cost calendar candidate, fit-only bins and frozen weighted objective. |
+| 13 | New observable future queries | None | Define novelty beyond existing queries and censoring. |
+| 14 | Soft write to primary hidden state | PR7 adjacent, different mechanism | Source-bound replay and soft-write vs dense recurrence. |
+| 15 | Bounded group-robust objective | None | Fit-only group definition and one bounded objective change. |
+| 16 | CUSUM slow-memory adaptation | PR4 adjacent only | CUSUM vs age/EW activity on fixed shifts. |
+| 17 | Cross-stream event order | None | Antisymmetric area vs fixed lags and count/sum-preserving shuffle. |
+| 18 | Masked current-feature reconstruction | None | Control mask, normalization, skip paths on same student. |
+| 19 | CPC future input states | None | Same-sequence negatives, persistence control and same student. |
+| 20 | Distribution/dependency distillation | PR3 scaffold only | Output-only KD vs fixed distribution summary; preserve two outputs. |
+| 21 | ARTBP compensated truncated gradient | None | Exact BPTT toy parity first; high compute cost. |
+| 22 | Content-based prior-state retrieval | None | Bound memory; recency/taps/shuffled-key controls. |
+| 23 | Transition/cycle topology | PR15 adjacent only | Occupancy features do not establish cycle topology. |
+| 24 | Adaptive fast memory teacher | None | Reset semantics and final fixed student vs ordinary teacher. |
+| 25 | Input world model/internal rollouts | None | Beat persistence/one-step; control compounded error and student transfer. |
+
+The separate `MAXIM-MINIMAL-FAITHFUL-KD` entry also remains blocked on exact recipe and fold-clean ancestry; preserve raw family targets, coefficient sum 0.8125, seed-specific parents and organizer provenance. Do not call ordinary KD a faithful replication.
+
+## Queue order after access is restored
+
+1. Root verifies worker identity, live device UUIDs/busy processes, topology, driver/CUDA/PyTorch/NCCL, physical storage/scratch, cgroup delegation, scheduler and actual data availability. Preserve foreign jobs and existing F0/F1 claims.
+2. Complete the two-shape R4 F2 actual FP32 profile and issue the source/data/owner/resource receipt. If admitted, run only the two F2/seed1001 fits and fixed endpoint/grade from the pinned recipe; keep both arms matched.
+3. Bind one implemented experiment at a time into complete immutable one-GPU arm templates, controls, dependencies, source/input hashes, finite budgets, expected artifacts and profile receipts. Begin with independent, code-ready GRU mechanisms; do not batch all PR titles into job JSON.
+4. Add PR15 only after source/data manifests and an eight-device profile/projection. Add PR17 only after its PyTorch smoke, complete-profile and per-fold teacher/cache registry. Implement and test missing architectures/features before admitting their scientific fits.
+5. Preserve the CP30 30-cell-per-arm rule for confirmation, clean outer-fold ancestry, strict FP32, fixed endpoint and unchanged official grader. Small first-seed screens are exploratory only. The eight-GPU user authorization does not turn the 25-rank hypothesis list into 25 ready implementations.
+
+No external publication, rental, billing/account change or foreign-job mutation is part of this handoff. The current measured state is still zero remote commands and zero B300 fits.

+# PR15 geometry/discrete B300 review
+
+**Disposition:** source-level CPU gates pass on the full deployed source, including Torch CPU parity (6 passed in 3.98 seconds; receipt `/data/epanov_s/tabdata/receipts/pr15-cpu-tests-v2.log`). Conditional go for the new PR15 cohort remains subject to the two-worker-per-card density profile passing alongside healthy R01 workers. The feature implementation is causal and the four controls are width-matched. I found no feature-level reason to block the first fit. This is not a claim that PR15 improves prediction quality; the full preregistered matrix and grading still decide that. No full PR15 fits have started; I ran no SSH commands or GPU work.
+
+## Source and recipe
+
+The locally reviewed PR source package is commit `e238fc5c82ac8c4591f3ca3ef87c37b2b73b929e`, archive SHA256 `29fb624f73a4d6ca8dc38a428fb73fa7fec2c410617b18781c4e0a8d30506985`. Its 172 files match the package manifest by path, size, mode, and file hash. It contains source and experiment metadata, not market data, targets, caches, or pretrained weights. The deployed 172-file tree still needs to remain bound to this commit/package identity in each run receipt.
+
+The arm mapping is `baseline=all`, `moments=moments_only`, `dictionary=dictionary_only`, and `combined=none`. Each arm retains the same 60 geometry/discrete columns and the same 271-wide total input (112 raw + 99 event + 60 derived). The exact masks are respectively all 60, columns 20–59, columns 0–19, and no mask. The recipe uses fresh H512 × 1 GRUs, B8, 2,000-row chunks, three epochs, fixed epoch 2, no evaluation during fit, train+valid fit membership, WMSE/AdamW/OneCycle, learning rate 0.001, weight decay 0.01, gradient clip 1.0, deterministic strict FP32. `common.train_command` binds the split manifest, fold, seed, control, and these settings; `pair_identity` plus the frozen matrix defines the 30 common fold/seed pairs for each of the four arms.
+
+## Causality and controls
+
+The transform uses only the selected raw channels `(0, 3, 52, 55)` at the current row and earlier rows within that sequence. Cumulative mean, standard deviation, residual, atom occupancy, normalized value, current category, category occupancy, dominant-event share, and dwell time reset at sequence boundaries. The dictionary/vocabulary and arc/atom prior are fitted from fit-membership raw sequences; labels and masks are not inputs to this feature fit. The trainer integration fits preprocessing on training batches, with online normalization disabled by default. The resulting checkpoint carries the prior and the selected control for inference. The full-sequence `predict_run` path rebuilds the same features from the checkpoint. `StreamingResearchFeatures` explicitly rejects this mode, so current evidence supports full-sequence prediction only; it does not establish stateful streaming-serving parity.
+
+The audit-only CPU gates are in `context-followup/pr15_review_cpu_tests.py`. They check the NumPy transform against a separate row-wise oracle, suffix-mutation prefix invariance and per-sequence reset, exact 60-column mask partitions, all 120 matched arm/cell commands, profile attempt arithmetic, and Torch-vs-NumPy parity plus Torch prefix invariance. The corrected suite passed on the complete deployed source with Torch CPU enabled: 6 passed in 3.98 seconds, recorded at `/data/epanov_s/tabdata/receipts/pr15-cpu-tests-v2.log`.
+
+The first full-source run exposed a test-harness call error: the Torch feature function's fourth positional parameter is the output buffer, while `control` is fifth. The test now passes `control=...` explicitly. This was a reviewer-test API mistake, not a production-source finding; the corrected Torch gate has since passed on the B300 host.
+
+## Profile and launch binding
+
+The frozen profile command is the canonical `common.train_command(profile_id, fold, seed, "none")` with `--profile-steps 8 --profile-warmup 2`. The CLI flags count batches, despite `PROFILE_CONFIG` calling them “updates.” With 20,000 rows per sequence and 2,000-row TBPTT chunks, each B8 batch makes 10 optimizer attempts: the 2 warmup plus 8 measured batches therefore mean 100 total attempts, of which 80 are timed. The launcher should check actual `PROFILE_UPDATE_EVIDENCE` reports 100 attempts and finite completed updates, along with strict FP32 evidence; do not treat the labels in the profile config as 10 optimizer steps.
+
+The original `run_cell.py` must not be reused unchanged for this admission. It requires a clean Git checkout and exact project-root/path mounts, expects an eight-card profile receipt, schedules one fit per card, and does not bind CPU affinity or a safe per-process CUDA allocator limit. Those assumptions do not describe two new PR15 workers sharing each B300 with a live R01 worker. The bounded custom adapter should call the exact canonical builder and stages, not fork trainer or feature code:
+
+```python
+command = common.train_command(run_name, fold, seed, common.CONTROL_BY_ARM[arm])
+subprocess.run(command, cwd=pr15_root, env=slot_environment, check=True)
+```
+
+For profile workers, use the same builder with control `"none"`, then append `("--profile-steps", "8", "--profile-warmup", "2")`. Give each process its unique run/profile name, dedicated output/cache/scratch roots, explicit source/runtime hashes, disjoint CPU affinity, and a conservative explicit `WNN_GPU_MEMORY_BYTES`; the default allocator fraction is based on each process's observed free memory and is unsafe as a shared-card reservation. Keep one process on each assigned GPU slot and verify aggregate memory, finite-update evidence, and R01 health before admitting the remaining cohort. After each fit, call the canonical `common.prediction_command(name, fold)` and `common.score_command(name, fold)` serially before releasing that slot; preserve distinct run names for every arm/fold/seed and require artifact plus score receipts.
+
+The host-level cgroup/profile gates and the first real-shape concurrent profile are operational admission conditions, not feature review claims. Any profile instability or R01 degradation should pause the new cohort without touching R01 or foreign processes.

+# PR15: causal geometry/discrete
+
+This package is the complete source tree at `e238fc5c82ac8c4591f3ca3ef87c37b2b73b929e`, not the incomplete saved PR API payload. Its archive contains the full `src/`, `scripts/geometry_b300/`, canonical `train_rnn.py` / `predict_run.py` / `score_run.py`, the target/graph/split/portable-manifest helpers, four committed fold manifests, `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock`, and the exact PR/recipe/launch documentation. Use the archive and manifest beside this file.
+
+The original trainer flags are `--research-features causal_geometry_discrete` and `--research-feature-control all|moments_only|dictionary_only|none`. The runner maps `baseline→all`, `moments→moments_only`, `dictionary→dictionary_only`, and `combined→none`, keeping all arms at the same 271-wide model input (211 raw/event plus 60 geometry channels). It is a fresh H512×1 GRU with batch 8, chunk 2,000, strict FP32, WMSE, AdamW (`lr=.001`, `wd=.01`), OneCycle, clip 1, three epochs, and the fixed epoch-2 endpoint. It has no teacher or parent checkpoint dependency.
+
+The preregistered matrix is four arms × CP30: folds F0/F1 with seeds 1001–1008 and F2/F3 with seeds 1001–1007, for 120 fits in 15 eight-card waves. Before fits, the original profile gate measures two warmup and eight optimizer updates at H512×1 / batch 8 / chunk 2,000 / width 271 on each card. The original entrypoints are `scripts/geometry_b300/profile_all.sh`, then `scripts/geometry_b300/launch_wave.sh PAIR_A PAIR_B PROFILE_RECEIPT`; `run_cell.py` is the per-cell runner. These commands are source templates, not evidence that a B300 profile or fit has run.
+
+The launch document binds four fold JSONs and portable manifests to `datasets/train.parquet`, `datasets/valid.parquet`, and `cache/{train_targets,valid_targets,chains,chain_folds}.npz`. The package includes code to cache targets, construct `chains.npz`, build split manifests from graph/fold inputs, and create portable source registries. `chain_folds.npz` has no producer in this commit; use the verified canonical assignment supplied with the data. Do not silently regenerate it or accept different fold/source hashes as this original attempt. The package contains no raw data or cache arrays.
+
+The original shell wrappers select GPU indices 0–7 and launch eight profiles/cells concurrently. Bind those wrappers to current host paths and current per-card admission before use; the historical mount paths and profile schedule do not account for the present host's co-located jobs. PR15 records zero B300 profiles, fits, or optimizer steps.

+# PR17: causal local-trend teacher and distillation
+
+This package is the full Git source tree at `588b93f9c2ad7e53aac7b1e2a39f30c32047ea22`; the recipe names base `origin/research-team@1ff144e09`. It contains the full `src/`, the eight-file adapter delta (including `scripts/train_kalman_teacher.py`, checkpoint reconstruction in `predict_run.py`, and teacher validation/cache construction in `build_distill_cache.py`), canonical trainer/scorer, split/data helpers, committed folds, `pyproject.toml`, `uv.lock`, and PR/recipe documentation. Its tiny NumPy synthetic prototype/receipt is included and is not task or B300 evidence.
+
+The trainer wrapper accepts `--kalman-arm raw|ema|fixed|learned` and `--kalman-channels pilot4|all112`, then forwards the normal canonical trainer arguments. Direct teachers start from fresh weights, use canonical WMSE, H1024×2, batch 16, chunk 2,000, strict FP32, AdamW (`lr=.001`, `wd=.01`), OneCycle, clip 1, two epochs and the fixed epoch-1 endpoint. The direct matrix is four arms × two scopes × CP30 = 240 teacher fits. The required first profile is the learned `all112` H1024×2 shape with one warmup and four measured updates. The exact command template is in `recipe.json` under `commands.profile`; smoke is `scripts/train_kalman_teacher.py --synthetic-smoke --kalman-arm learned --kalman-channels all112`. Neither was run during packaging.
+
+The full proposal adds three H256×2 student arms (90 more fits), making 330 total. Their epoch-1 endpoint uses a same-fold four-family distillation blend: `strong`, `full_finetuned`, `raw_wmse`, and `samefold_baseline`, with total coefficient 0.8125 and student alpha 0.5. The treatment replaces only `samefold_baseline` with the matching fold/seed learned smoother at the same coefficient. The draft does not supply the required clean per-fold/seed teacher registry, run IDs, fixed epochs, coefficients, checkpoint/provenance hashes, or split-bound cache identities. Do not admit student cells until that lineage is reconstructed and validated. No checkpoints or teacher caches are in the package.
+
+The four committed fold manifests are included. The package contains source helpers for targets, graph and split handling, but no raw parquet, target/cache arrays, or `chain_folds.npz`; that last file has no producer in this source commit and must come from the verified canonical data package. PR17 records no B300 profile, task fit, teacher cache, or grade. The eager Python time loop and the 448 added channels for `all112` remain actual-device memory/throughput risks.
+
+## Independent implementation audit
+
+At pinned commit `588b93f9c2ad7e53aac7b1e2a39f30c32047ea22`, the local-trend recurrence is causal and its posterior state is carried across chunks and reset for each sequence batch. The current synthetic smoke is much narrower than the planned trainer: it checks a 24-row prefix and reset, finite loss, and only the learned level-process-noise gradient. It does not compare against an independent Kalman oracle, test chunk continuation, perform an optimizer update, or round-trip a checkpoint through prediction/cache export.
+
+Before admitting PR17 fits, fix/test the wrapper's precision guard: it accepts duplicate flags such as `--precision fp32 --precision bf16` because it checks only the first occurrence, while the canonical parser uses the last. Explicitly assert highest float32 matmul precision in addition to disabling TF32. Bind `src/wnn/features.py` and `src/wnn/data.py` into model-source identity; validate recipe-critical checkpoint arguments in the cache builder; and export with explicit `--epoch 1` so prediction sidecars bind the fixed checkpoint checked by the cache builder. The current source identity covers the adapter and GRU core but omits those imported feature/data semantics.
+
+Minimum bounded gates: (1) CPU scalar float64 Kalman oracle for fixed/learned filters, including the current initialization convention (seed level from x0 and then assimilate x0), covariance/finite/gradient checks, one-shot versus carried-chunk equality, independent sequence reset and future-prefix invariance; (2) tiny CPU shared-trainer update with FP32/autocast/TF32 assertions, finite gradients, learned-Q/R update, fixed epoch1 save/reload and prediction-sidecar hash checks; (3) synthetic B300 all112 shape at B16×T2000, input211, H1024×2, strict FP32 actual forward/backward/AdamW, one warmup plus an update, peak memory/timing/headroom capture, then streamed T20000 prediction and checkpoint/export parity. The required student source registry remains absent and must bind per-cell source run IDs, epochs, weights, checkpoint/provenance hashes and fold lineage before any KD cache or student fit.

+# Fourth-process throughput measurement
+
+The latest user request authorizes testing increased concurrency on the existing eight B300s. Root uses the existing single SSH operator console; the 24 full fits and their frozen recipes remain unchanged.
+
+The bounded `tabdata-density4-v3` unit overlays one canonical PR15 profile on GPU2 and GPU7, using disjoint CPU pairs 56/58 and 61/63. Each profile completes two warmup plus 64 timed outer batches, or 660 optimizer updates and 528 sequences, under strict FP32. GPU2 has a deep R01 fit and two PR15 fits; GPU7 has a wide R01 fit and two PR15 fits. Foreign workloads are preserved.
+
+The measurement compares 125 seconds of existing three-process progress with progress during the fourth process. Existing actor rates come from completed batch increments and log timestamps. Since canonical profiles suppress progress lines, an independent 0.5-second observer records loader-to-completed-update walltime. The added actor's rate includes all warmup and overhead. Aggregate rates include R01 contention; epoch-budget-normalized rates are reported separately. This short engineering test cannot establish sustained eight-GPU throughput or model quality.
+
+Remote evidence lives under `/data/epanov_s/tabdata/state/density4-v3`; executable measurement, observer and postprocessor live under `runtime/density4-v3`. At 2026-10-18 21:17:18 UTC both profile actors had entered training; no concurrency decision or queue handoff had yet occurred. The existing frozen controllers remain unchanged.
+
+Failed startup attempts are retained: v1 omitted a required workspace argument and started no CUDA actor; v2 detected generated Python bytecode before profiling and started no CUDA actor. The two bytecode files created by the first attempt were quarantined with hashes under `state/density4-v1/generated_bytecode`, and v3 disables bytecode writing. No tracked training source was changed.
+
+The separate [successor preparation](../density4_v1/r01_successor/README.md) preserves pending-cell ownership until an exact process-identity and journal/process/workspace reconciliation transfers it. Healthy initial fits retain their original processes, CPUs and inherited deadlines.
+
+The [exact deployed R01 v4 source snapshot](../deployed_review_v4/README.md) supplies the actual controller, actor adapters and postprocessing contracts for successor review, with source pins verified against the server manifest. It deliberately excludes bulk canonical fold payloads.
+
+## Observed measurements and allocation decision
+
+The fourth-PR15 overlay completed both finite 660-update profiles. Its unit failed only in a postprocessor that expected progress lines suppressed by canonical profile mode. The retained [walltime analysis](observed/state/density4-v3/WALLTIME_RESULT.json) uses actual incumbent progress and external walltime instead: aggregate sequences/s rose 5.75% on GPU2 and 2.80% on GPU7, while the incumbent R01 fit slowed 14.30% and 22.76%. This allocation does not address the campaign's R01 tail.
+
+The mixed overlay instead adds a wide R01 to a deep incumbent on GPU2 and a deep R01 to a wide incumbent on GPU7. Both completed 340 finite strict-FP32 updates. Its older a266 profile source omitted a newer resource-evidence marker, so that unit also retains an explicit failed postprocessor status. [Feasibility](observed/state/density4-r01-v1/FEASIBILITY.json) records conservative startup-inclusive aggregate R01 rates of 4.61766 versus 2.64930 sequences/s on GPU2 (+74.30%) and 4.65409 versus 3.35526 on GPU7 (+38.71%). PR15 service slowed approximately 22–24% in those windows.
+
+The [joint fit-queue projection](observed/state/density4-r01-v1/FIT_QUEUE_PROJECTION.json) estimates the remaining R01 tail at 38.46h rather than 50.15h and PR15 at 26.48h rather than 20.52h: approximately 23.3% less time for the slower fit queue. This is a provisional two-GPU engineering projection, excluding export, scoring, repair and nonpreemptive scheduling overhead; it is not an observed campaign duration or a promised ETA.
+
+[Resource reconciliation](observed/state/density4-r01-v1/RESOURCE_RECONCILIATION.json) binds actual profile PIDs, finite update counters, source/recipe/device/CPU identities and normal trainer returns while retaining both failed postprocessing records. Profile peak memory and profile OOM counters were unavailable after their cgroup disappeared and remain null. Original R01 memory events were zero, all 16 original PR15 full fits completed, and the three foreign vLLM clients remained alive. Fresh per-unit hard limits, RSS/OOM counts, host memory and live process-group observations are required for scaleout.
+
+The separately corrected [PR15 queue](../pr15_queue_v2/README.md) recovered all 16 original endpoints without retraining and launched the remaining 104-cell successor at two PR15 workers per GPU. The selected target composition is two R01 (one wide, one deep) plus two PR15 actors per GPU; its actual launch/adoption status belongs in the successor and live-status receipts.
+
+## Eight-GPU follow-up after actual scaleout
+
+The root-owned [read-only observer](observed/runtime/density4-followup-v1/observe.py) samples real batch-index increments and log timestamps every five seconds under a separate1GiB/swap0/32-task CPU unit bounded to30 minutes. It starts no training/GPU actor and sends no process signals. The [complete warm-window receipt](observed/state/density4-followup-v1/WARM_WINDOW.json) contains all24 incumbent actors before scaleout and all32 after scaleout, using a baseline ending before the start gate and a follow-up beginning120 seconds after it. Each actor needs at least two distinct progress points spanning35 seconds. Startup warming and short-window variability remain limitations.
+
+In that all-eight-GPU window, aggregate R01 service rose from24.150 to38.677 sequences/s (+60.15%), while PR15 service fell from51.596 to39.229 sequences/s (about24% slower). This is measured reallocation toward the longer R01 queue, not a60% reduction in total campaign time. Summed raw sequence service across both families rose only about2.9%; their epoch budgets and model work differ.
+
+The [live queue forecast](observed/state/density4-followup-v1/LIVE_QUEUE_FORECAST.json), around22:09 UTC, uses the actual remaining batch counts of the180 frozen cells, excludes the16 already completed original fits, and serializes each measured GPU/arm or GPU/lane slot. It estimates35.19h for the R01 fit tail and28.58h for PR15. First original wide R01 fits had about1.6–1.8h of fitting left, and the active PR15 wave about3.6–3.8h. These estimates exclude export, scoring, repair and phase/scheduling overhead and may change with future contention; they are not completion observations. The all-eight-GPU follow-up refines, rather than replaces the historical evidence for, the earlier two-GPU38.46h projection.

+"""Observe actual cohort progress without changing training processes."""
+import json,re,time,subprocess
+from pathlib import Path
+ROOT=Path('/data/epanov_s/tabdata')
+DEST=ROOT/'state/density4-followup-v1'
+PAT=re.compile(r'ep ([0-9]+) batch ([0-9]+)/([0-9]+).*?seq/s ([0-9.]+)')
+DEST.mkdir(exist_ok=False)
+start=time.monotonic()
+with (DEST/'progress.jsonl').open('x',buffering=1) as out:
+ while time.monotonic()-start<1800:
+  row={'observed_unix':time.time(),'progress':{}}
+  for state in ['r01-execution-v4','r01-density4-v1','pr15-execution-v2']:
+   for p in (ROOT/'state'/state/'logs').glob('*.log'):
+    try:
+     matches=PAT.findall(p.read_text(errors='replace'))
+     if matches:
+      ep,b,total,reported=matches[-1]
+      row['progress'][p.stem]={'state':state,'batch_index':int(ep)*int(total)+int(b),'log_mtime':p.stat().st_mtime,'reported_seq_s':float(reported)}
+    except FileNotFoundError:pass
+  out.write(json.dumps(row,separators=(',',':'))+'\n')
+  time.sleep(5)

+                              pr15_family_rate_change_fraction=after_pr15/before_pr15-1,

+    result=dict(schema="tabdata-density4-r01-feasibility.v1",time_unix=time.time(),results=results,

+                limitations="Short sequential windows, reused earlier baseline and sparse incumbent progress. Added actor rate includes unit startup, warmup and process exit. Engineering feasibility only, not sustained makespan or quality evidence.",
+                scientific_recipe_unchanged=True,original_fits_and_controllers_untouched=True)
+    p=S/"FEASIBILITY.json";p.write_text(json.dumps(result,indent=2)+"\n")

+

+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import hashlib
+import json
+import math
+from pathlib import Path
+
+ROOT = Path("/data/epanov_s/tabdata")
+STATE = ROOT / "state/density4-v3"
+
+
+def record(text: str, label: str) -> dict:
+    """Require exactly one canonical profile evidence record."""
+    rows = [json.loads(line[len(label) + 1:]) for line in text.splitlines() if line.startswith(label + " ")]
+    if len(rows) != 1:
+        raise ValueError(f"Expected one {label}, got {len(rows)}")
+    return rows[0]
+
+
+def progress_rate(points: list[dict], start: float, end: float) -> dict:
+    """Compute observed useful work, rejecting sparse or stale progress."""
+    rows = [row for row in points if start <= row["time_unix"] <= end]
+    if len(rows) < 3:
+        raise ValueError(f"Insufficient time-aligned progress points: {len(rows)}")
+    if rows[0]["time_unix"] - start > 90 or end - rows[-1]["time_unix"] > 90:
+        raise ValueError("Original training did not span the comparison window")
+    span = rows[-1]["time_unix"] - rows[0]["time_unix"]
+    batches = rows[-1]["batch_index"] - rows[0]["batch_index"]
+    if span < 75 or batches <= 0:
+        raise ValueError("Progress window is short or non-monotonic")
+    return dict(sequences_per_second=batches * 8 / span, observed_seconds=span,
+                completed_batches=batches, completed_optimizer_updates=batches * 10,
+                first_unix=rows[0]["time_unix"], last_unix=rows[-1]["time_unix"])
+
+
+def main() -> None:
+    """Evaluate four-process throughput with existing R01 contention included."""
+    baseline = json.loads((STATE / "BASELINE.json").read_text())
+    samples = json.loads((STATE / "SAMPLES.json").read_text())
+    observer = json.loads((STATE / "OBSERVER.json").read_text())["rows"]
+    results = {}
+    for gpu in ("2", "7"):
+        timing = observer[gpu]
+        start, end = timing["training_seen"], timing["completed_seen"]
+        span = end - start
+        if not 120 < span < 600:
+            raise ValueError(f"Invalid observed profile interval: {span}")
+        text = (STATE / "logs" / f"gpu{gpu}.log").read_text()
+        updates = record(text, "PROFILE_UPDATE_EVIDENCE")
+        resource = record(text, "PROFILE_RESOURCE_EVIDENCE")
+        profile = record(text, "PROFILE")
+        envelope = record(text, "PROCESS_ENVELOPE")
+        if updates["optimizer_completed_updates"] != 660 or not updates["valid_for_throughput"]:
+            raise ValueError("Profile did not complete 660 finite optimizer updates")
+        if resource["precision"] != "fp32" or resource["matmul_tf32"] or resource["cudnn_tf32"] or resource["float32_matmul_precision"] != "highest":
+            raise ValueError("Strict FP32 contract failed")
+        during = {name: progress_rate(samples[name], start, end) for name in baseline[gpu]}
+        fourth = dict(sequences_per_second=66 * 8 / span, completed_batches=66,
+                      completed_optimizer_updates=660, observed_seconds=span)
+        before = sum(row["sequences_per_second"] for row in baseline[gpu].values())
+        after = sum(row["sequences_per_second"] for row in during.values()) + fourth["sequences_per_second"]
+        r01_name = next(name for name in during if name.startswith("tabdata_b300_r01"))
+        r01_change = during[r01_name]["sequences_per_second"] / baseline[gpu][r01_name]["sequences_per_second"] - 1
+        before_progress = sum(row["sequences_per_second"] / (6 if name == r01_name else 3) for name, row in baseline[gpu].items())
+        after_progress = sum(row["sequences_per_second"] / (6 if name == r01_name else 3) for name, row in during.items()) + fourth["sequences_per_second"] / 3
+        results[gpu] = dict(baseline_three=baseline[gpu], existing_during_four=during,
+                            added_profile=fourth, before_sequences_per_second=before,
+                            after_sequences_per_second=after, aggregate_gain_fraction=after / before - 1,
+                            epoch_budget_normalized_gain_fraction=after_progress / before_progress - 1,
+                            r01_rate_change_fraction=r01_change, profile=profile, updates=updates,
+                            resource=resource, envelope=envelope, window_start_unix=start, window_end_unix=end)
+        if not all(math.isfinite(value) for value in (before, after, after_progress, before_progress)):
+            raise ValueError("Nonfinite throughput evidence")
+    receipt = dict(schema="tabdata-density4-walltime.v1", results=results,
+                   interpretation="Engineering throughput only; existing actor rates from progress-log intervals. Added actor rate is all 528 sequences over observed loader-to-complete walltime, including warmup/overhead. Two GPUs and one short window do not establish sustained 8-GPU throughput.",
+                   scientific_recipe_changed=False, original_controllers_untouched=True,
+                   source_hashes={str(path.relative_to(ROOT)): hashlib.sha256(path.read_bytes()).hexdigest() for path in (ROOT / "runtime/density4-v3/bench.py", ROOT / "runtime/density4-v3/observe.py", Path(__file__))})
+    output = STATE / "WALLTIME_RESULT.json"
+    with output.open("x") as stream:
+        json.dump(receipt, stream, indent=2)
+        stream.write("\n")
+    print(json.dumps(receipt))
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import hashlib
+import json
+import os
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import Iterable
+
+GPU_UUIDS = (
+    "GPU-daf615f5-ea55-860a-bfe1-41c36ab96c3e",
+    "GPU-25ae492c-db98-e1ae-0f5e-c56365a422c7",
+    "GPU-df6fe7d0-64e5-7af2-467d-c1699cb6fc67",
+    "GPU-76951d88-add3-0d6b-5bee-c0390915ca47",
+    "GPU-e6d65cb1-aba4-14f5-d4e5-bf24ef1ee3d8",
+    "GPU-1fc4d921-dc78-6711-c2a8-ec0589b7f106",
+    "GPU-2913ac69-eccb-63b0-1112-e09ea9598b57",
+    "GPU-be85f55c-71a1-f389-eeed-55c63a0e3ce7",
+)
+ARMS = ("baseline", "moments", "dictionary", "combined")
+CONTROLS = ("all", "moments_only", "dictionary_only", "none")
+JOB_FIELDS = (
+    "id",
+    "pair_index",
+    "fold",
+    "seed",
+    "arm",
+    "control",
+    "gpu_index",
+    "gpu_uuid",
+    "lane",
+    "cpus",
+)
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class ProcIdentity:
+    """Kernel identity needed to distinguish a live process from a reused PID."""
+
+    pid: int
+    state: str
+    parent_pid: int
+    process_group: int
+    session: int
+    start_ticks: int
+
+
+def _object(value: object, label: str) -> dict[str, object]:
+    """Require a JSON object at an untrusted state boundary."""
+    if not isinstance(value, dict) or any(not isinstance(key, str) for key in value):
+        raise ValueError(f"{label} must be a JSON object with string keys")
+    return value
+
+
+def _original_cpu_pair(gpu: int, lane: int) -> list[int]:
+    """Reproduce PR15 v1's frozen CPU assignment for its two existing lanes."""
+    start = 16 + (gpu % 4) * 8 + lane * 4 + (gpu // 4)
+    return [start, start + 2]
+
+
+def _expected_job(pair_index: int, arm_index: int) -> dict[str, object]:
+    """Build one queue record using the frozen v1 panel mapping."""
+    fold, seed = pair_index % 4, 1001 + pair_index // 4
+    position = fold * 4 + arm_index
+    gpu, lane = (position + pair_index // 4) % 8, position // 8
+    arm, control = ARMS[arm_index], CONTROLS[arm_index]
+    return {
+        "id": f"pr15_b300_v1_{arm}_f{fold}_s{seed}",
+        "pair_index": pair_index,
+        "fold": fold,
+        "seed": seed,
+        "arm": arm,
+        "control": control,
+        "gpu_index": gpu,
+        "gpu_uuid": GPU_UUIDS[gpu],
+        "lane": lane,
+        "cpus": _original_cpu_pair(gpu, lane),
+    }
+
+
+def load_panel(path: Path) -> tuple[dict[str, object], ...]:
+    """Verify the persisted v1 panel against its exact 120-cell identity."""
+    payload = _object(json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")), "panel")
+    raw_jobs = payload.get("jobs")
+    if not isinstance(raw_jobs, list) or len(raw_jobs) != 120:
+        raise ValueError("source panel must contain exactly 120 jobs")
+    jobs = tuple(_object(row, "panel job") for row in raw_jobs)
+    expected = tuple(
+        _expected_job(pair_index, arm_index)
+        for pair_index in range(30)
+        for arm_index in range(4)
+    )
+    actual_by_id = {str(job.get("id")): job for job in jobs}
+    if len(actual_by_id) != 120:
+        raise ValueError("source panel contains duplicate or missing job IDs")
+    if tuple(actual_by_id[str(job["id"])] for job in expected) != expected:
+        raise ValueError("source panel differs from the frozen v1 cell/GPU mapping")
+    return jobs
+
+
+def read_started_events(
+    path: Path, jobs: Iterable[dict[str, object]]
+) -> dict[str, tuple[int, dict[str, object]]]:
+    """Read fsynced v1 starts strictly; an incomplete ledger blocks takeover."""
+    expected = {str(job["id"]): job for job in jobs}
+    raw = path.read_bytes()
+    if raw and not raw.endswith(b"\n"):
+        raise ValueError("v1 event journal has a partial final record")
+    starts: dict[str, tuple[int, dict[str, object]]] = {}
+    for line_number, line in enumerate(raw.splitlines(), 1):
+        event = _object(json.loads(line), f"event line {line_number}")
+        if event.get("event") != "fit_started":
+            continue
+        job = _object(event.get("job"), f"fit_started job on line {line_number}")
+        job_id, pid = job.get("id"), event.get("pid")
+        if not isinstance(job_id, str) or type(pid) is not int or pid <= 0:
+            raise ValueError(f"invalid fit_started identity on line {line_number}")
+        if job_id not in expected or job != expected[job_id]:
+            raise ValueError(f"fit_started event does not match frozen panel: {job_id}")
+        if job_id in starts:
+            raise ValueError(f"duplicate fit_started event for {job_id}")
+        starts[job_id] = (pid, job)
+    return starts
+
+
+def claimed_jobs(
+    jobs: Iterable[dict[str, object]],
+    starts: dict[str, tuple[int, dict[str, object]]],
+    old_work_root: Path,
+) -> tuple[set[str], set[str]]:
+    """Exclude every started cell and every pre-existing work directory."""
+    panel_ids = {str(job["id"]) for job in jobs}
+    if not set(starts) <= panel_ids:
+        raise ValueError("start ledger includes cells outside the original panel")
+    directories: set[str] = set()
+    for job_id in panel_ids:
+        work = old_work_root / job_id
+        if work.is_symlink():
+            raise ValueError(f"worker path is a symlink; manual review required: {work}")
+        if work.exists():
+            if not work.is_dir():
+                raise ValueError(f"worker path is not a directory: {work}")
+            directories.add(job_id)
+    return set(starts) | directories, directories - set(starts)
+
+
+def pending_by_gpu(
+    jobs: Iterable[dict[str, object]], claimed: set[str]
+) -> dict[int, list[dict[str, object]]]:
+    """Keep original cell-to-GPU placement and return only never-claimed cells."""
+    pending = {gpu: [] for gpu in range(8)}
+    for job in jobs:
+        job_id, gpu = str(job["id"]), int(job["gpu_index"])
+        if job_id not in claimed:
+            pending[gpu].append(job)
+    if any(len(queue) > 15 for queue in pending.values()):
+        raise ValueError("pending queue count exceeds the frozen 15 cells per GPU")
+    return pending
+
+
+def density4_cpu_pair(gpu: int) -> tuple[int, int]:
+    """Assign the new lane to its disjoint 48-63 CPU pair, NUMA-interleaved."""
+    if not 0 <= gpu < 8:
+        raise ValueError(f"invalid GPU index: {gpu}")
+    first = 48 + (gpu % 4) * 4 + (gpu // 4)
+    return first, first + 2
+
+
+def slot_table(
+    jobs: Iterable[dict[str, object]],
+) -> tuple[dict[str, object], ...]:
+    """Build 24 PR15 slots while retaining the v1 placements for lanes 0-1."""
+    slot_cpus: dict[tuple[int, int], list[int]] = {}
+    for job in jobs:
+        key = (int(job["gpu_index"]), int(job["lane"]))
+        cpus = job["cpus"]
+        if not isinstance(cpus, list) or key in slot_cpus and slot_cpus[key] != cpus:
+            raise ValueError(f"inconsistent original CPU slot: {key}")
+        slot_cpus[key] = cpus
+    slots: list[dict[str, object]] = []
+    for gpu in range(8):
+        for lane in range(3):
+            cpus = slot_cpus[(gpu, lane)] if lane < 2 else list(density4_cpu_pair(gpu))
+            slots.append(
+                {"gpu_index": gpu, "gpu_uuid": GPU_UUIDS[gpu], "lane": lane, "cpus": cpus}
+            )
+    flattened = [cpu for slot in slots for cpu in slot["cpus"]]
+    if len(slots) != 24 or len(flattened) != len(set(flattened)):
+        raise ValueError("successor CPU slots are not disjoint")
+    if set(flattened) != set(range(16, 64)):
+        raise ValueError("successor CPU slot union must be exactly 16-63")
+    return tuple(slots)
+
+
+def campaign_deadline(
+    launch_time_unix: float,
+    wall_cap_seconds: int = 120 * 3600,
+    parent_deadline_unix: float | None = None,
+) -> float:
+    """Return the inherited absolute deadline without resetting the v1 wall cap."""
+    if launch_time_unix <= 0 or wall_cap_seconds <= 0:
+        raise ValueError("launch time and wall cap must be positive")
+    deadline = launch_time_unix + wall_cap_seconds
+    return min(deadline, parent_deadline_unix) if parent_deadline_unix else deadline
+
+
+def can_start_cell(
+    deadline_unix: float,
+    now_unix: float,
+    forecast_seconds: float,
+    per_fit_cap_seconds: float = 12 * 3600,
+) -> bool:
+    """Require the conservative fit projection and original 12-hour cap to fit."""
+    if forecast_seconds <= 0 or per_fit_cap_seconds <= 0:
+        raise ValueError("fit forecast and per-fit cap must be positive")
+    return deadline_unix - now_unix >= max(forecast_seconds, per_fit_cap_seconds)
+
+
+def parse_proc_stat(text: str, pid: int) -> ProcIdentity:
+    """Parse Linux proc stat fields while tolerating spaces and ')' in comm."""
+    right = text.rfind(")")
+    left = text.find("(")
+    if left < 0 or right <= left or not text[:left].strip().isdigit():
+        raise ValueError("malformed /proc/PID/stat record")
+    actual_pid = int(text[:left].strip())
+    fields = text[right + 1 :].split()
+    if actual_pid != pid or len(fields) <= 19 or len(fields[0]) != 1:
+        raise ValueError("/proc/PID/stat PID or field count is invalid")
+    return ProcIdentity(
+        pid=pid,
+        state=fields[0],
+        parent_pid=int(fields[1]),
+        process_group=int(fields[2]),
+        session=int(fields[3]),
+        start_ticks=int(fields[19]),
+    )
+
+
+def capture_pidfd(
+    pid: int, proc_root: Path = Path("/proc")
+) -> tuple[int, ProcIdentity]:
+    """Open a stable process handle and reject a PID reused during inspection."""
+    if not hasattr(os, "pidfd_open"):
+        raise OSError("Linux pidfd_open is required for PR15 worker adoption")
+    before = parse_proc_stat((proc_root / str(pid) / "stat").read_text(), pid)
+    pidfd = os.pidfd_open(pid)
+    try:
+        after = parse_proc_stat((proc_root / str(pid) / "stat").read_text(), pid)
+        if before.start_ticks != after.start_ticks:
+            raise ProcessLookupError(f"PID {pid} changed identity during pidfd capture")
+    except BaseException:
+        os.close(pidfd)
+        raise
+    return pidfd, after
+
+
+def sha256_bytes(payload: bytes) -> str:
+    """Hash a captured command line without retaining its potentially sensitive text."""
+    return hashlib.sha256(payload).hexdigest()

+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import math
+
+GIB = 1024**3
+MEMORY_LIMIT = 192 * GIB
+MEMORY_ADMISSION_CEILING = 180 * GIB
+WORKER_RSS_LIMIT = 24 * GIB
+DISK_FLOOR = 8 * GIB
+PID_LIMIT = 512
+OOM_KEYS = ("high", "max", "oom", "oom_group_kill", "oom_kill")
+
+
+def validate_aggregate_resources(
+    receipt: dict[str, object], baseline_oom: dict[str, int]
+) -> None:
+    """Fail closed unless combined old/new/R01 resource evidence is admissible."""
+    if receipt.get("scope") != "b300_campaign_aggregate":
+        raise ValueError("resource receipt must cover old, successor and R01 scopes")
+    if receipt.get("ancestor_limits_verified") is not True:
+        raise ValueError("shared ancestor cgroup limits were not verified")
+    numeric_limits = {
+        "memory_max_bytes": MEMORY_LIMIT,
+        "memory_swap_max_bytes": 0,
+        "pids_max": PID_LIMIT,
+    }
+    for key, expected in numeric_limits.items():
+        value = receipt.get(key)
+        if type(value) is not int or value != expected:
+            raise ValueError(f"aggregate {key} must equal {expected}")
+    current = receipt.get("memory_current_bytes")
+    swap_current = receipt.get("memory_swap_current_bytes")
+    tasks = receipt.get("pids_current")
+    disk_free = receipt.get("disk_free_bytes")
+    for key, value in (
+        ("memory_current_bytes", current),
+        ("memory_swap_current_bytes", swap_current),
+        ("pids_current", tasks),
+        ("disk_free_bytes", disk_free),
+    ):
+        if type(value) is not int or value < 0:
+            raise ValueError(f"aggregate {key} must be a nonnegative integer")
+    if current >= MEMORY_ADMISSION_CEILING:
+        raise ValueError("aggregate memory is at or above the 180 GiB stop-admission gate")
+    if swap_current != 0 or tasks >= PID_LIMIT:
+        raise ValueError("aggregate swap or task count violates the execution envelope")
+    if disk_free < DISK_FLOOR:
+        raise ValueError("less than 8 GiB of physical disk space remains")
+    events = receipt.get("oom_events")
+    if not isinstance(events, dict):
+        raise ValueError("aggregate OOM counters are missing")
+    for key in OOM_KEYS:
+        value, baseline = events.get(key), baseline_oom.get(key)
+        if type(value) is not int or type(baseline) is not int or value != baseline:
+            raise ValueError(f"OOM counter changed during the observed interval: {key}")
+    rss = receipt.get("worker_group_rss_bytes")
+    if not isinstance(rss, dict) or not rss:
+        raise ValueError("worker process-group RSS evidence is required")
+    for group_id, value in rss.items():
+        if not isinstance(group_id, str) or type(value) is not int or value < 0:
+            raise ValueError("worker RSS records must bind names to nonnegative byte counts")
+        if value > WORKER_RSS_LIMIT:
+            raise ValueError(f"worker group exceeds the 24 GiB RSS cap: {group_id}")
+
+
+def validate_absolute_deadlines(
+    *,
+    old_unit_started_unix: float,
+    current_unix: float,
+    job_started_unix: dict[str, float],
+    campaign_cap_seconds: int = 120 * 3600,
+    fit_cap_seconds: int = 12 * 3600,
+) -> tuple[float, dict[str, float]]:
+    """Carry original wall deadlines forward instead of granting a fresh budget."""
+    values = (old_unit_started_unix, current_unix)
+    if any(not math.isfinite(value) or value <= 0 for value in values):
+        raise ValueError("deadline timestamps must be finite positive Unix times")
+    if campaign_cap_seconds <= 0 or fit_cap_seconds <= 0:
+        raise ValueError("campaign and fit caps must be positive")
+    campaign_deadline = old_unit_started_unix + campaign_cap_seconds
+    if current_unix >= campaign_deadline:
+        raise TimeoutError("the original campaign deadline has expired")
+    deadlines: dict[str, float] = {}
+    for job_id, started in job_started_unix.items():
+        if not math.isfinite(started) or started <= 0:
+            raise ValueError(f"invalid original fit start time for {job_id}")
+        deadline = started + fit_cap_seconds
+        if current_unix >= deadline:
+            raise TimeoutError(f"the original per-fit deadline has expired: {job_id}")
+        deadlines[job_id] = min(deadline, campaign_deadline)
+    return campaign_deadline, deadlines
+
+
+def can_admit_new_fit(
+    *,
+    now_unix: float,
+    campaign_deadline_unix: float,
+    conservative_fit_seconds: float,
+    fit_cap_seconds: float = 12 * 3600,
+) -> bool:
+    """Do not admit a fit unless its measured forecast and 12-hour cap fit."""
+    values = (now_unix, campaign_deadline_unix, conservative_fit_seconds, fit_cap_seconds)
+    if any(not math.isfinite(value) or value <= 0 for value in values):
+        raise ValueError("fit admission timestamps and budgets must be positive")
+    return campaign_deadline_unix - now_unix >= max(
+        conservative_fit_seconds, fit_cap_seconds
+    )

+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import os
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from pathlib import Path
+
+from handoff_core import ProcIdentity, parse_proc_stat, sha256_bytes
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class ProcSnapshot:
+    """Read-only identity and ownership view of one process in the old unit."""
+
+    identity: ProcIdentity
+    cgroup_path: str
+    argv: tuple[str, ...]
+    cmdline_sha256: str
+
+
+def cgroup_path(pid: int, proc_root: Path = Path("/proc")) -> str:
+    """Return one process's unified cgroup path or reject ambiguous cgroup data."""
+    records = (proc_root / str(pid) / "cgroup").read_text().splitlines()
+    unified = [line.partition("::")[2] for line in records if line.startswith("0::")]
+    if len(unified) != 1 or not unified[0].startswith("/"):
+        raise ValueError(f"PID {pid} has no unique cgroup-v2 path")
+    return unified[0]
+
+
+def _argv(pid: int, proc_root: Path) -> tuple[tuple[str, ...], bytes]:
+    """Read command arguments without decoding arbitrary bytes lossily."""
+    raw = (proc_root / str(pid) / "cmdline").read_bytes()
+    return tuple(part.decode("utf-8", errors="replace") for part in raw.split(b"\0") if part), raw
+
+
+def snapshot_pid(pid: int, proc_root: Path = Path("/proc")) -> ProcSnapshot:
+    """Take a stable double-read snapshot for PID-reuse-safe reconciliation."""
+    process_dir = proc_root / str(pid)
+    first = parse_proc_stat((process_dir / "stat").read_text(), pid)
+    argv, raw_cmdline = _argv(pid, proc_root)
+    owner = cgroup_path(pid, proc_root)
+    last = parse_proc_stat((process_dir / "stat").read_text(), pid)
+    if first.start_ticks != last.start_ticks:
+        raise ProcessLookupError(f"PID {pid} changed during /proc inspection")
+    return ProcSnapshot(last, owner, argv, sha256_bytes(raw_cmdline))
+
+
+def unit_members(unit_name: str, proc_root: Path = Path("/proc")) -> tuple[ProcSnapshot, ...]:
+    """Enumerate current processes in one exact systemd unit, including zombies."""
+    target = f"{unit_name}.service"
+    snapshots: list[ProcSnapshot] = []
+    for entry in proc_root.iterdir():
+        if not entry.name.isdigit():
+            continue
+        try:
+            item = snapshot_pid(int(entry.name), proc_root)
+        except (FileNotFoundError, ProcessLookupError, PermissionError):
+            continue
+        path_parts = item.cgroup_path.rstrip("/").split("/")
+        if path_parts[-1:] == [target]:
+            snapshots.append(item)
+    return tuple(sorted(snapshots, key=lambda item: item.identity.pid))
+
+
+def parse_worker_args(argv: tuple[str, ...]) -> dict[str, str]:
+    """Parse the exact PR15 worker CLI fields used to recover an unjournaled spawn."""
+    script_indices = [i for i, token in enumerate(argv) if token.endswith("/worker.py")]
+    if len(script_indices) != 1:
+        raise ValueError("process is not one unique PR15 worker.py invocation")
+    values: dict[str, str] = {}
+    tokens = argv[script_indices[0] + 1 :]
+    for index, token in enumerate(tokens[:-1]):
+        if token.startswith("--"):
+            if token in values:
+                raise ValueError(f"duplicate worker argument: {token}")
+            values[token] = tokens[index + 1]
+    required = ("--root", "--name", "--fold", "--seed", "--control", "--gpu", "--cpus", "--work", "--mode")
+    if set(values) != set(required) or values["--mode"] != "fit":
+        raise ValueError("worker command is incomplete or is not a full fit")
+    return values
+
+
+def worker_job_id(snapshot: ProcSnapshot, unit_name: str) -> str | None:
+    """Identify a live full-fit worker in the exact old unit; ignore all others."""
+    if snapshot.cgroup_path.rstrip("/").split("/")[-1:] != [f"{unit_name}.service"]:
+        return None
+    if not snapshot.argv:
+        return None
+    try:
+        return parse_worker_args(snapshot.argv)["--name"]
+    except ValueError:
+        return None
+
+
+def require_controller_identity(
+    snapshot: ProcSnapshot,
+    *,
+    expected_pid: int,
+    expected_start_ticks: int,
+    expected_unit: str,
+    command_marker: str,
+    must_be_stopped: bool = False,
+) -> None:
+    """Guard a future SIGSTOP/retirement action with exact PID, start and unit."""
+    identity = snapshot.identity
+    if identity.pid != expected_pid or identity.start_ticks != expected_start_ticks:
+        raise ValueError("controller PID was reused or its start identity changed")
+    if snapshot.cgroup_path.rstrip("/").split("/")[-1:] != [f"{expected_unit}.service"]:
+        raise ValueError("controller PID is outside the frozen PR15 systemd unit")
+    if not any(command_marker in token for token in snapshot.argv):
+        raise ValueError("controller command line does not match the frozen controller")
+    if must_be_stopped and identity.state not in {"T", "t"}:
+        raise ValueError("old controller is not confirmed stopped")
+
+
+def grouped_members(snapshots: tuple[ProcSnapshot, ...]) -> dict[int, tuple[int, ...]]:
+    """Group a unit's PIDs by process group so no worker descendant is orphaned."""
+    groups: dict[int, list[int]] = {}
+    for snapshot in snapshots:
+        groups.setdefault(snapshot.identity.process_group, []).append(snapshot.identity.pid)
+    return {group: tuple(sorted(pids)) for group, pids in sorted(groups.items())}

+The following preserves the pre-deployment boundary, superseded by the deployment receipts above: at preparation time, no R01 adoption or successor `fit_started` count is claimed here. +python3 successor.py --authority "$AUTHORITY" prepare
+python3 successor.py --authority "$AUTHORITY" freeze
+python3 successor.py --authority "$AUTHORITY" run

+`prepare` creates a fresh isolated state directory. `freeze` stops only the old R01 MainPID after rechecking its PID, start ticks, cgroup and command hash, and writes a durable receipt; if verification fails after SIGSTOP, it attempts SIGCONT through the pinned pidfd. `run` requires that receipt, re-reconciles the original cohort, adopts its eight workers, and starts only panel cells whose run directory and other evidence remain absent. +Local checks cover scheduling uniqueness, process identity parsing, authority receipt gates, and CLI import/help. Deployment review must regenerate the flat Python file manifest after the final freeze and run the same tests in the remote Linux environment. This packet does not connect to SSH, stop a process, or start an experiment by itself.

+"""Read-only process and artifact reconciliation for R01-v4 takeover."""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import importlib
+import os
+import sys
+import time
+from collections.abc import Callable
+from pathlib import Path
+from typing import Any
+
+from frozen_panel import (
+    FIT_CAP_SECONDS,
+    R01_PANEL_SHA256,
+    parse_journal,
+    progress_state,
+    read_object,
+    sha256_file,
+    validate_panel,
+    verify_frozen_packet,
+)
+from proc_snapshot import ProcSnapshot, grouped_members, require_controller_identity, unit_members
+
+
+def _process_jobs(
+    snapshots: tuple[ProcSnapshot, ...],
+    jobs: tuple[dict[str, Any], ...],
+    *,
+    controller_pid: int,
+    expected_unit: str,
+    affinity_reader: Callable[[int], set[int]],
+    start_records: dict[str, dict[str, Any]],
+) -> dict[str, ProcSnapshot]:
+    """Map every unit process group to one exact old controller or fit actor."""
+    groups = grouped_members(snapshots)
+    by_pid = {item.identity.pid: item for item in snapshots}
+    output: dict[str, ProcSnapshot] = {}
+    for pgid, pids in groups.items():
+        if controller_pid in pids:
+            if len(pids) != 1:
+                raise ValueError("old controller shares its process group with another process")
+            continue
+        leaders = [
+            by_pid[pid]
+            for pid in pids
+            if by_pid[pid].identity.pid == pgid
+            and any(by_pid[pid].argv == tuple(str(token) for token in job["argv"]) for job in jobs)
+        ]
+        if not leaders:
+            started_job = next(
+                (
+                    job
+                    for job_id, start in start_records.items()
+                    if start.get("pid") == pgid
+                    for job in jobs
+                    if str(job["id"]) == job_id
+                ),
+                None,
+            )
+            if started_job is not None and pgid in by_pid:
+                leaders = [by_pid[pgid]]
+        if len(leaders) != 1:
+            raise ValueError(f"unexplained process group in frozen unit {expected_unit}: {pgid}")
+        worker = leaders[0]
+        job = next(
+            (job for job in jobs if tuple(str(token) for token in job["argv"]) == worker.argv),
+            None,
+        )
+        if job is None:
+            job = next(
+                job
+                for job_id, start in start_records.items()
+                if start.get("pid") == worker.identity.pid
+                for job in jobs
+                if str(job["id"]) == job_id
+            )
+        active_members = [
+            by_pid[pid] for pid in pids if by_pid[pid].identity.state not in {"Z", "X"}
+        ]
+        if active_members:
+            _validate_worker_binding(
+                next(
+                    (item for item in active_members if item.identity.pid == pgid),
+                    active_members[0],
+                ),
+                job,
+            )
+        job_id = str(job["id"])
+        if job_id in output:
+            raise ValueError(f"duplicate live process group for {job_id}")
+        for pid in pids:
+            member = by_pid[pid]
+            if member.identity.state in {"Z", "X"}:
+                continue
+            try:
+                affinity = affinity_reader(pid)
+            except (AttributeError, ProcessLookupError, PermissionError) as error:
+                raise ValueError(f"cannot verify old worker CPU affinity: {pid}") from error
+            if affinity != set(job["cpu_ids_initial"]):
+                raise ValueError(f"old worker process affinity differs from panel: {job_id}")
+        output[job_id] = worker
+    return output
+
+
+def _validate_worker_binding(snapshot: ProcSnapshot, job: dict[str, Any]) -> None:
+    """Bind an old worker's live environment and working directory to its frozen cell."""
+    environment = snapshot.environment
+    expected = {
+        "CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES": str(job["gpu_uuid"]),
+        "WNN_RUN_DIR": str(job["run_dir"]),
+        "WNN_GPU_MEMORY_BYTES": str(6 * 1024**3),
+        "WNN_THREADS": "2",
+        "OMP_NUM_THREADS": "2",
+        "MKL_NUM_THREADS": "2",
+        "OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS": "2",
+        "NUMEXPR_NUM_THREADS": "2",
+        "NVIDIA_TF32_OVERRIDE": "0",
+        "TORCH_ALLOW_TF32_CUBLAS_OVERRIDE": "0",
+        "PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE": "1",
+    }
+    if any(environment.get(key) != value for key, value in expected.items()):
+        raise ValueError(f"old worker environment differs from the frozen runtime: {job['id']}")
+    root = Path(str(job["run_dir"])).parent.parent
+    if snapshot.cwd != str(root):
+        raise ValueError(f"old worker cwd differs from the project root: {job['id']}")
+    argv = tuple(str(token) for token in job["argv"])
+    for flag, expected_path in (
+        ("--source-root", root / "runtime" / "source-a266-lf-subset-v1"),
+        ("--data-root", root / "data"),
+    ):
+        try:
+            observed = Path(argv[argv.index(flag) + 1])
+        except (ValueError, IndexError) as error:
+            raise ValueError(f"frozen actor argv omits {flag}: {job['id']}") from error
+        if observed != expected_path:
+            raise ValueError(f"old worker {flag} differs from the frozen project data: {job['id']}")
+
+
+def _validate_finished_fit(root: Path, packet: Path, job: dict[str, Any]) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    """Use the packet's exact fit and ancestry validators for a non-live claimed cell."""
+    control = packet / "control"
+    resolved = control.resolve(strict=True)
+    sys.path.insert(0, str(resolved))
+    try:
+        fit_stage = importlib.import_module("fit_stage")
+        postprocess_fit = importlib.import_module("postprocess_fit")
+        fit_receipt = fit_stage._validate_fit_receipt(job)
+        binding = postprocess_fit._fit_binding(root, job)
+    finally:
+        if sys.path and sys.path[0] == str(resolved):
+            sys.path.pop(0)
+    return {
+        "status": "validated_fixed_epoch5_fit",
+        "job_id": str(job["id"]),
+        "fit_receipt_sha256": binding["fit_receipt_sha256"],
+        "checkpoint_sha256": binding["checkpoint_sha256"],
+        "split_sha256": binding["split_sha256"],
+        "producer_status": fit_receipt["status"],
+        "exit_code": "not_observable_for_nonchild_process",
+    }
+
+
+def proc_start_unix(snapshot: ProcSnapshot, proc_root: Path = Path("/proc")) -> float:
+    """Convert a stable Linux start-tick identity to Unix time."""
+    boot_time = next(
+        (
+            line.split()[1]
+            for line in (proc_root / "stat").read_text(encoding="ascii").splitlines()
+            if line.startswith("btime ")
+        ),
+        None,
+    )
+    if boot_time is None:
+        raise ValueError("/proc/stat has no boot-time record")
+    return float(boot_time) + snapshot.identity.start_ticks / os.sysconf("SC_CLK_TCK")
+
+
+def reconcile_state(
+    *,
+    root: Path,
+    packet: Path,
+    state: Path,
+    unit: str,
+    main_pid: int,
+    main_start_ticks: int,
+    main_cgroup: str,
+    main_cmdline_sha256: str,
+    main_cmd_marker: str,
+    proc_root: Path = Path("/proc"),
+    affinity_reader: Callable[[int], set[int]] | None = None,
+    must_be_stopped: bool = True,
+) -> dict[str, Any]:
+    """Require a stopped exact main process and recover every claimed old R01 cell."""
+    reader = affinity_reader or getattr(os, "sched_getaffinity", None)
+    if reader is None:
+        raise OSError("Linux CPU affinity inspection is required for takeover")
+    manifest = verify_frozen_packet(packet)
+    panel = read_object(packet / "PANEL.json")
+    jobs = validate_panel(panel, root)
+    members = unit_members(unit, proc_root)
+    main = next((item for item in members if item.identity.pid == main_pid), None)
+    if main is None:
+        raise ValueError("frozen R01 MainPID is absent from its exact systemd unit")
+    require_controller_identity(
+        main,
+        expected_pid=main_pid,
+        expected_start_ticks=main_start_ticks,
+        expected_unit=unit,
+        command_marker=main_cmd_marker,
+        must_be_stopped=must_be_stopped,
+    )
+    if main.cgroup_path != main_cgroup:
+        raise ValueError("frozen R01 MainPID cgroup path differs from root authority")
+    if main.cmdline_sha256 != main_cmdline_sha256:
+        raise ValueError("frozen R01 MainPID command bytes differ from root authority")
+    if sha256_file(packet / "PANEL.json") != R01_PANEL_SHA256:
+        raise ValueError("R01 panel changed after freeze authority was sealed")
+    events = parse_journal(state / "events.jsonl", jobs)
+    progress = progress_state(state / "PROGRESS.json", jobs)
+    live = _process_jobs(
+        members,
+        jobs,
+        controller_pid=main_pid,
+        expected_unit=unit,
+        affinity_reader=reader,
+        start_records=events["starts"],
+    )
+    live_processes: dict[str, ProcSnapshot] = {}
+    zombie_processes: dict[str, ProcSnapshot] = {}
+    for job_id, snapshot in live.items():
+        group = [
+            item
+            for item in members
+            if item.identity.process_group == snapshot.identity.process_group
+        ]
+        if group and all(item.identity.state in {"Z", "X"} for item in group):
+            zombie_processes[job_id] = snapshot
+        else:
+            live_processes[job_id] = snapshot
+        started = events["starts"].get(job_id)
+        if started is not None and started["pid"] != snapshot.identity.pid:
+            raise ValueError(f"live worker PID differs from journal for {job_id}")
+    claimed = set(events["referenced"]) | set(progress["claimed"])
+    evidence: dict[str, list[str]] = {str(job["id"]): [] for job in jobs}
+    for job in jobs:
+        job_id = str(job["id"])
+        paths = {
+            "run_dir": Path(str(job["run_dir"])),
+            "log": state / "logs" / f"{job_id}.log",
+            "producer_receipt": Path(str(job["run_dir"])) / "producer_receipt.json",
+            "export": root / "exports" / job_id,
+            "grade": root / "grades" / f"seed{job['seed']}" / f"fold{job['fold']}",
+        }
+        for label, path in paths.items():
+            if path.is_symlink():
+                raise ValueError(f"R01 cell evidence path is a symlink: {path}")
+            if path.exists():
+                evidence[job_id].append(label)
+                claimed.add(job_id)
+        if job_id in live_processes:
+            evidence[job_id].append("live_exact_argv")
+            claimed.add(job_id)
+        if job_id in zombie_processes:
+            evidence[job_id].append("zombie_worker_group")
+            claimed.add(job_id)
+    pending = sorted(str(job["id"]) for job in jobs if str(job["id"]) not in claimed)
+    if progress["pending"] is not None and progress["pending"] < len(pending):
+        raise ValueError("R01 progress pending count is below reconciled zero-evidence cells")
+    job_by_id = {str(job["id"]): job for job in jobs}
+    live_details: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
+    for job_id, snapshot in live_processes.items():
+        started_unix = proc_start_unix(snapshot, proc_root)
+        live_details[job_id] = {
+            "pid": snapshot.identity.pid,
+            "start_ticks": snapshot.identity.start_ticks,
+            "pgid": snapshot.identity.process_group,
+            "state": snapshot.identity.state,
+            "started_unix": started_unix,
+            "deadline_unix": started_unix + FIT_CAP_SECONDS,
+            "argv_sha256": snapshot.cmdline_sha256,
+            "job": job_by_id[job_id],
+        }
+    terminal: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
+    finished_claims = claimed - set(live_processes)
+    for job_id in sorted(finished_claims):
+        job = job_by_id[job_id]
+        try:
+            binding = _validate_finished_fit(root, packet, job)
+        except Exception as error:
+            raise ValueError(
+                f"claimed non-live R01 cell lacks a validated terminal fit: {job_id}"
+            ) from error
+        terminal[job_id] = binding
+    if set(zombie_processes) - set(terminal):
+        raise ValueError("zombie old-worker leader lacks its validated terminal fit receipt")
+    return {
+        "schema": "tabdata-r01-v4-adoption-snapshot.v2",
+        "observed_unix": time.time(),
+        "unit": unit,
+        "packet_manifest_sha256": sha256_file(packet / "EXECUTION_MANIFEST.json"),
+        "panel_sha256": sha256_file(packet / "PANEL.json"),
+        "main": {
+            "pid": main.identity.pid,
+            "start_ticks": main.identity.start_ticks,
+            "state": main.identity.state,
+            "cgroup_path": main.cgroup_path,
+            "cmdline_sha256": main.cmdline_sha256,
+        },
+        "journal_sha256": events["sha256"],
+        "claimed": sorted(claimed),
+        "pending": pending,
+        "live": live_details,
+        "terminal_fits": terminal,
+        "evidence": evidence,
+        "failure_events": events["failures"],
+        "progress_stop_admission": progress["stop"],
+        "event_start_ids": sorted(events["starts"]),
+        "unlogged_live_ids": sorted(set(live_processes) - set(events["starts"])),
+        "zero_evidence_count": len(pending),
+        "source_manifest_sha256": manifest.get("source_manifest_sha256"),
+    }
+
+
+def validate_initial_takeover(
+    snapshot: dict[str, Any],
+    jobs: tuple[dict[str, Any], ...],
+    *,
+    require_stopped: bool = True,
+) -> None:
+    """Fail closed unless the exact eight-fit v4 first wave remains the only claim."""
+    expected_live = {str(job["id"]) for job in jobs if job["seed"] == 1003}
+    expected_all = {str(job["id"]) for job in jobs}
+    live = snapshot.get("live")
+    main = snapshot.get("main")
+    pending = snapshot.get("pending")
+    claimed = snapshot.get("claimed")
+    evidence = snapshot.get("evidence")
+    if not isinstance(live, dict) or set(live) != expected_live or len(live) != 8:
+        raise ValueError("takeover is limited to all eight live seed-1003 R01 workers")
+    expected_state = {"T", "t"} if require_stopped else {"R", "S", "D", "I"}
+    if not isinstance(main, dict) or main.get("state") not in expected_state:
+        expectation = "stopped" if require_stopped else "running"
+        raise ValueError(f"the exact old R01 controller must be {expectation} for this phase")
+    if not isinstance(claimed, list) or set(claimed) != expected_live:
+        raise ValueError("takeover requires exactly the original eight claimed R01 cells")
+    if (
+        not isinstance(pending, list)
+        or set(pending) != expected_all - expected_live
+        or len(pending) != 52
+    ):
+        raise ValueError("takeover requires all 52 remaining cells to have zero prior evidence")
